title: Agent-workspace tmp has no retention routine; system-cleanup.sh targets obsolete paths and is unscheduled
body:
## Problem

The framework tells agents to put temporary artifacts under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}` (`.agents/AGENTS.md`, "Tool and file discipline"), but no routine prunes that directory. Session scratch directories (issue bodies, snapshots, PR drafts) build up indefinitely. Agents also cannot delete them: the command policy blocks `rm -rf` under home. So sessions end up telling the user to delete them by hand, which contradicts the rule that cleanup is routine-owned.

The only retention code is `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh`, and it targets obsolete paths:
- `TMP_DIR="$HOME/.agents/tmp"`, not the agent-workspace tmp directory
- `LOG_DIR="$HOME/.agents/logs"`, `AGENT_DIR="$HOME/.agents"`, `PROJECT_DIR="$HOME/git/aidevops"` (lowercase `git`)
- Nothing schedules or calls it: `rg -l "system-cleanup.sh" .agents setup.sh` matches only the script itself.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `rg -n "TMP_DIR=|PROJECT_DIR=" .agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh`, then `rg -l "system-cleanup.sh" .agents setup.sh`

**Actual output**: `TMP_DIR="$HOME/.agents/tmp"` and `PROJECT_DIR="$HOME/git/aidevops"`; the only reference is the script itself. Meanwhile an interactive session's `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/<session-scratch>/` directory is never removed, and the agent cannot remove it (`rm -rf` is blocked by command policy).

**Expected**: a scheduled routine prunes stale agent-workspace tmp entries, so sessions can report temp cleanup as automatic.

## Proposed fix

- Point retention at `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`. Prune top-level entries older than a configurable retention period (default 7 days, by mtime). Skip `session-checkpoints/` and anything newer than the retention period. Skip entries referenced by a live session lease or lock if such a registry exists. Use the existing trash-backed deletion helper if one exists instead of raw `rm -rf`.
- Either fix `system-cleanup.sh` (paths from `shared-constants.sh`, drop the stale `PROJECT_DIR`) and schedule it, or fold the tmp pruning into the existing pulse cleanup (`.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`). Prefer whichever already runs on a schedule. Scheduled job naming: launchd `sh.aidevops.<name>`.
- Dry-run by default when invoked manually. Log deletions to `~/.aidevops/logs/`.

## Verification

- Run `shellcheck` and `linters-local.sh --changed`.
- Runtime: create an old scratch directory (`touch -t` to more than 8 days ago) and a fresh one under the tmp root. Run the routine in dry-run mode, then for real. Only the old directory is removed, and `session-checkpoints/` is untouched.
- Run the existing `rg -l "pulse-cleanup|system-cleanup" .agents/scripts/tests` matches.

Files: `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`, and scheduling in `setup.sh` / routines only if a new job is needed.

title: approval-helper.sh: formatting-only shfmt cleanup of the signed-comment classification loop
body:
## Problem

`.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` has `shfmt` formatting drift in the signed-comment classification loop around lines 1627-1660. Single-line `case` arms and `{ …; return N; }` groups are compact, while `shfmt` expects them expanded. Any later edit to this trust-boundary file that runs `shfmt -w` produces unrelated formatting noise in the diff, which makes security review harder.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `shfmt -d .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`

**Actual output**: one diff hunk expanding `VERIFIED) printf 'VERIFIED\n'; return 0 ;;` into a multi-line arm, and a second hunk expanding four `[[ "$saw_…" -eq 0 ]] || { printf '…\n'; return N; }` lines into multi-line groups (return codes 6, 4, 3 and 7).

**Expected**: `shfmt -d` prints nothing.

## Proposed fix

- Apply `shfmt -w .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` with the repository's shfmt settings (check `.editorconfig`), in a formatting-only PR with no behaviour change.
- Confirm that the diff only touches whitespace and line breaks: `git diff -w --ignore-blank-lines` should show just the brace and semicolon restructuring.
- Optionally check whether other `approval-*.sh` files have the same drift (`shfmt -l .agents/scripts/approval-*.sh`) and include them if the diff stays formatting-only.

## Verification

- `shfmt -d .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` prints nothing.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` is clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-batch.sh` still pass.

Files: `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`.

title: Completion guidance: routine-owned cleanup gets one no-action line, never a user task
body:
## Problem

Interactive sessions keep telling the user to clean up things a routine already owns: deferred worktrees and session scratch directories. The guidance says routine-owned cleanup should be silent (`.agents/reference/session.md` Session Lifecycle, and `workflows/full-loop.md` "User-facing completion"). But in practice:
- the agent attempted `worktree-helper.sh remove` on a merged, cleanup-deferred worktree, and when the guarded removal refused, told the user to handle it or run `worktree-helper.sh clean`;
- when the command policy blocked `rm -rf` on a session scratch directory, the agent turned that into a "left for you" item.

The maintainer's preferred behaviour: cleanup happens through routines once sessions close. At most, a completion message should say so in one line that makes clear no action is needed. It should never present routine cleanup as a user task.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: complete an interactive `/full-loop` merge whose cleanup is deferred (`LIFECYCLE_STATE=CLEANUP_DEFERRED`), in a session that also wrote scratch files under the agent-workspace tmp directory.

**Actual output**: the completion message included "Left for you (optional): … worktree … `worktree-helper.sh clean` … delete `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/<scratch>/` when convenient".

**Expected**: either nothing about cleanup, or one line such as `Cleanup: the worktree is removed automatically by a routine after this session closes; no action needed.`

## Change

- `.agents/AGENTS.md` (Completion messages): routine-owned cleanup gets one no-action line unless user action is required or work is at risk (+15 bytes; the file stays under the 24000-byte ratchet).
- `.agents/reference/session.md` (Session Lifecycle): do not attempt deferred cleanup; guarded-removal refusals and command-policy deletion blocks are not user tasks; give the no-action example line; user action only for failures that require it or put unpublished work at risk.
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` (User-facing completion): the same no-action line replaces "silent".
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh`: literals updated, plus new assertions for the no-action line and the blocked-deletion case.

Related: #32485 adds the missing retention routine for agent-workspace tmp, so scratch-directory cleanup is also routine-owned in practice.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh` → PASS
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` → exit 0; markdownlint 0 issues; `wc -c .agents/AGENTS.md` → 23948 (limit 24000)

title: Enforce parent acceptance receipts for subagent results via a hook (1.6% coverage today)
body:
## What

Make parent acceptance of subagent results observable by default: prompt for, or infer safely, an `aidevops_objective_receipt` decision after each completed child Task, instead of relying on the model to call the tool voluntarily.

## Why

The tiering and effort review under #32484 (2026-09-27) found that only **8 of 504** recorded interactive subagent dispatches (1.6%) had a parent acceptance/repair receipt. Without receipts, routing feedback cannot tell a verified child contribution from host completion. That blocks evidence-based decisions on whether cheaper child routes (Luna / Sol low) are good enough. See `.agents/reference/model-effort-evaluation.md` for the coverage limits this causes.

Deterministic prompt rules should migrate to hooks (`.agents/AGENTS.md` "Quality and diagnostics"; `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`).

## How

1. Read `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/objective-receipt-tool.mjs` (tool contract: never infers acceptance from host completion) and its registration in `index.mjs:429` / `v2.mjs:303`.
2. Read the Task tool after-hook path in `subagent-effort-escalation.mjs` (`host_outcome` recording) to find where a child completion is known together with its `callID`/child session ID.
3. Implement the lowest-friction enforcement that keeps the tool's "explicit decision only" contract:
   - Preferred: after a completed child Task, append a short synthetic reminder to the tool output. It should name the `contribution_id`/`run_id` values the parent needs so a receipt call is a copy, not a lookup.
   - Do **not** auto-record `accepted_*`. Recording `unknown` when a session ends without a decision is acceptable if it is clearly labelled as inferred absence.
4. Keep the reminder short (token cost on every child return) and skip it for pinned or advisory-only children if that is already distinguishable.
5. Add an entry to `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf` marking this rule as migrated.

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-escalation.mjs` (or a new small module it calls, to avoid Qlty complexity regressions).
- REFERENCE `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/objective-receipt-tool.mjs`, `observability.mjs` (`recordObjectiveDecision`).
- EDIT `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`.

## Acceptance

- Each completed child Task output carries a receipt reminder with the identifiers needed.
- No acceptance is inferred from host completion.
- The existing plugin tests pass (`node --test` with explicit files: `test-subagent-effort.mjs`, `test-observability-routing-join.mjs`, `test-routing-feedback.mjs`).
- A local qlty smell check (`qlty smells --no-snippets <changed files>`) shows no new findings.
- After one week, the receipt coverage ratio (`runtime_events` receipts ÷ interactive child dispatches in `llm-requests.db`) is reported on this issue or in `model-effort-evaluation.md`.

title: OpenCode V2 parity: load framework AGENTS.md, sanitize service restart env, leave Tabby recovery dirs
body:
## Problem

After the GH#32444 release (v3.37.1/v3.37.2), a user test showed OpenCode V2 (`opencode2`) does not load everything OpenCode 1 loads, and one V2 session skipped the aidevops greeting.

Evidence gathered from the V2 session database, the V2 server log and the shared plugin log:

1. **V2 never loads the framework user guide.** OpenCode 1 loads `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` (~24 KB, the Framework Rules) through `instructions` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. The isolated V2 config (`~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/config/opencode/opencode.json`) only has `plugins`, and there is no `AGENTS.md` in the V2 config dir. V2 sessions therefore run without the framework rules (git safety, completion discipline, security rules). V2 does watch and load `<V2 config>/opencode/AGENTS.md`: a probe with a symlinked canary `AGENTS.md` in a copied config home produced a `core/instructions` entry and the canary reply.
2. **The V2 background service inherits the environment of whatever process restarted it.** `_restart_opencode_v2_service_after_deploy` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`) runs `opencode2 service restart`, and the shim passes the full caller environment through. The live service after the last deploy carries an unrelated OpenCode 1 session's `OPENCODE_PID`, `AIDEVOPS_OPERATION_ID`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pinned to a days-old 3.34.33 runtime bundle. If a deploy runs from a headless context, `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`/`AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`/`OPENCODE_HEADLESS` leak in too, and `isHeadless()` then suppresses the greeting (and changes other interactive behaviour) for every V2 session until the next restart. The affected session's request had 5 redistributed system blocks versus 6 for otherwise identical sessions; the ~1.6K-char difference matches the greeting block. The previous service process is gone, so its exact environment cannot be confirmed.
3. **`opencode2` starts inside Tabby recovery marker directories.** OpenCode 1 reports `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-tabby-recovery/<session>/` to Tabby as the tab's current directory (OSC 1337). Tabs opened from that tab start their shell there, and `opencode2` then creates a session in the marker directory. That session misses the project `AGENTS.md` and runs tools in the wrong directory. The OpenCode 1 launcher resolves markers (`resolve_tabby_recovery` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh`); the V2 shim does not.
4. **Greeting skips are not observable.** `ttsrSystemTransform` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs`) silently omits the greeting when disabled or when `shouldInjectGreeting` returns false, so the cause of a missing greeting cannot be read from logs.

## Proposed fix

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` (or the V2 setup path in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`): ensure `<V2 config>/opencode/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md`. Never replace a user-authored regular file.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh` `_setup_write_opencode_v2_shim`:
  - for service lifecycle commands (`service …`, `serve --service`), drop session-scoped and headless variables before exec;
  - when started inside a validated recovery marker directory, `cd` to the marker's recorded project directory (never resume the OpenCode 1 session in V2);
  - bump a shim version marker so existing shims are regenerated.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` `_restart_opencode_v2_service_after_deploy`: restart with the same sanitized environment.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs`: log one line per session when the greeting is skipped, with the reason (`disabled`/`headless-or-child`).
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`: update the greeting-source comment (the V2 config `AGENTS.md` is the framework guide, not a greeting fallback, so the plugin greeting stays the default).

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` covers the symlink, the regular-file guard, the shim version marker, service environment sanitization, and recovery-directory redirection.
- Relevant plugin tests for the greeting-skip log.
- Live check after deploy:
  - a fresh `opencode2` session's `instruction_state` includes `core/instructions` containing the framework guide;
  - `opencode2 service restart` from a shell with `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1` yields a service without that variable (`ps -E`);
  - `opencode2` launched from a marker directory opens in the project directory;
  - the greeting still appears exactly once.

Ref #32444

title: fix(opencode): context7 on-demand MCP activation and V2 terminal title version suffix
body:
## What

Two gaps found while verifying OpenCode V1 1.18.32 / V2 2.0.3 with aidevops v3.37.2:

1. **Context7 cannot be connected on demand.** `context7` is registered disabled (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`, remote `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`) but has no `activationAgent`, so `aidevops_mcp` rejects it and no Context7 tools are reachable in V1 or V2 sessions. Build+ lists `context7` as its library-docs path.
2. **V2 terminal title lacks `· AIDevOps <version>`.** V1 stores the suffix in the session title (`session-title-suffix.mjs`). V2 titles come from `v2-plugin/tui.mjs`, which renders status dots but no version suffix.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: in an `opencode2` (or `opencode`) session, ask "start the context7 MCP"; observe the Tabby tab title in `opencode2`.

**Actual output**: agent reports `aidevops_mcp` only accepts playwriter, posthog, playwright, quickfile, mobile-mcp, blender-lab, affinity-studio, freecad, ableton, davinci-resolve, backblaze-b2; sidebar lists `context7 Disabled`. V2 tab title is `🟢 Greeting` while V1 shows `Greeting · AIDevOps 3.37.2`.

## How

- `mcp-registry.mjs`: give `context7` `activationAgent: "context7"`, `agentSource: ["tools","context","context7.md"]`, `modelTier: "simple"`, untrusted-content and CLI-fallback guidance. It stays disconnected at startup and tools stay scoped to the `context7` agent, matching the PostHog pattern.
- `v2-plugin/tui.mjs`: append the suffix (via `withAidevopsTitleSuffix`) to the terminal title only (V2 session titles double as tab labels), reading `~/.aidevops/agents/VERSION` at most once per minute.

## Acceptance

- `@context7` can `aidevops_mcp connect context7` and use `context7_*` tools; other agents do not get them.
- V2 terminal title shows `<dot> <title> · AIDevOps <version>`.

## Verification

`node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-context7-mcp-registry.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-tui-title.mjs`

title: bug(release): exact-tag deployment gate rejects active bundle when main advanced before publication merge
body:
## Problem

The post-release exact-tag deployment gate rejects a valid active runtime bundle when `main` moved forward while a release was in progress. Publication succeeds, but the release lane stays in `exact-tag-deployment` with no terminal receipt, and the local agents stay on the previous VERSION label.

## Reproducer

Observed on v3.37.3, source PR #32474. Release tag `dbfed4421` (base `7d6e75664`). Before publication merged, another session deployed the runtime bundle from `main` commit `b91c0a895` (GH#32488), which changed `.agents/AGENTS.md`. Publication PR #32497 merged as `8179fe777`, with parents `8c70b3879` (main, which descends from `b91c0a895`) and `c89b5ad98` (release side).

**Symptom command**:

```
aidevops release reconcile 32474
```

**Actual output**:

```
Post-release squash recovery rejected active source b91c0a895dff: changed path is not identical in release: .agents/AGENTS.md
Post-release deployment gate rejected active source b91c0a895dff: it is neither ancestry-related nor a lane-authorized squash-integrated source
PARTIAL RELEASE SUCCESS: GitHub release v3.37.3 remains published; post-publication gates failed
```

**Expected output**:

The gate recognises the protected integration merge and takes the `stale_runtime=1` path (exit 76 plus a recorded `stale_runtime_recovery`). The next deployment from a descendant then converges the lane, and #32474's release receipt moves to `release:published`.

Impact note: until #32512 (merged in #32513), this left the public lane in `exact-tag-deployment` and blocked `aidevops update` and auto-update for every git install.

## Root cause

In `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh:747-757`, `_verify_protected_release_integration` accepts only a protected-main merge whose two parents are exactly `active_sha` and `release_sha`. When `main` advances past the active source before the publication merge, the integration merge's first parent is a descendant of `active_sha`, not `active_sha` itself. The check then falls through to `_verify_squash_integrated_active_source` (lines 761-793), which rightly rejects the post-base path changes.

## Expected

If both `active_sha` and `release_sha` are ancestors of protected `origin/main`, and a protected merge exists whose first-parent history contains `active_sha` and whose other parent contains `release_sha`, treat the active source as release-integrated. That is the `stale_runtime=1` path, which redeploys from the integrated tree. Unrelated or unmerged active sources must still be rejected.

## Worker Guidance

- **Files:** `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` (`_verify_protected_release_integration`). Tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`, which already covers these error messages.
- **Pattern:** keep the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` semantics. Require protected `origin/main` ancestry for both SHAs. Accept a merge `M` on `--ancestry-path release..main` where `release` is an ancestor of one parent and `active` is an ancestor of the other.
- **Verification:**
  - Add a regression fixture: active commit on main, then main advances, then a publication merge of the release branch. The gate must pass.
  - Keep a negative fixture where the active source is not on protected main. It must still be rejected.
  - Then `aidevops release reconcile 32474` should converge the lane for v3.37.3.

Related: #32474 (source PR), #32497 (publication PR).

## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #32520)

The previous worker's PR #32520 (`GH#32506: fix(release): accept integrated active ancestor after main advances`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).
The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (2 files touched).

### Files in the conflicting PR

```
.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh
.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh
```

### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `88c51b8ce758c1833dc1739f904058c991f1a274`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/32520/head:recovered-32520
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick 88c51b8ce758c1833dc1739f904058c991f1a274
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

title: fix(release): stale-runtime deferral should accept active runtime that is an ancestor of the integration merge's mainline parent
body:
## Problem

The v3.37.3 exact-tag deployment (source PR #32474) deadlocked. The active runtime was hot-deployed from `b91c0a895` (GH#32488). That commit is an ordinary mainline commit after the release base `7d6e75664`. Further mainline merges landed (`5e7246d5d`, `7c6b3d2ba`, `8c70b3879`) before protected-main PR #32497 merged the signed release commit `dbfed4421` in merge `8179fe777`.

`_verify_protected_release_integration` (`.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh:727`) grants the `stale-runtime/v1` deferral only when the active SHA is **exactly** a parent of the integration merge. Reconcile therefore failed with "neither ancestry-related nor a lane-authorized squash-integrated source". That left the lane in `exact-tag-deployment`, which blocks:

- generic `setup.sh` / `aidevops update` ("Active exact-tag release deployment blocks generic setup");
- every new release (the v3.37.4 release of PR #32493).

The GH#32103 design addressed the same deadlock class seen at v3.34.7, but only for the zero-intervening-merge topology.

## Fix

Accept the deferral when the active runtime is an ancestor of, or equal to, the integration merge's non-release parent. That parent must be reachable from freshly fetched protected main. The integration merge then contains the entire active runtime, so converging on protected main cannot downgrade it. The deferral itself deploys nothing, and every other invariant stays unchanged: signed tag, lane CAS, exact release parent, unreachable-main rejection.

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` (`_verify_protected_release_integration`)
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`:
  - the intervening-merge topology now defers;
  - a new rejection case: active runtime merged to main only after the integration merge.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`
- ShellCheck
- `linters-local.sh --changed`
- After merge, from a current linked worktree:
  1. run `aidevops release reconcile 32474` via the worktree helper;
  2. expect the `stale-runtime/v1` deferral, then runtime convergence and a terminal receipt;
  3. release PR #32493.

title: OpenCode: 18 registered MCPs have no on-demand activation path or Build+ route (macos-automator, chrome-devtools, sentry, ...)

## What

Of the 29 MCPs aidevops registers in OpenCode (all correctly start disconnected, which the MCP sidebar shows as `Disabled`), only 11 can be connected on demand. The other 18 have no `activationAgent`/`agentSource` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`, so `aidevops_mcp` rejects them and Build+ cannot reach them. It also cannot delegate to an agent that has their tools, because the Task tool exposes no such agent types. Build+ therefore does not know these capabilities exist when a task needs them.

Related: #32499 fixes `context7` only, using the same pattern. Do not duplicate that part.

## Observed failure (2026-09-26)

A user asked Build+ to test a packaged Electron app's native macOS folder picker "with computer-use". Build+ answered that no computer-use capability was available. `macos-automator` (AppleScript/JXA) was installed but unreachable:

- Registry entry at `mcp-registry.mjs:273-282` has no `activationAgent`.
- `aidevops_mcp` accepted only: playwriter, posthog, playwright, quickfile, mobile-mcp, blender-lab, affinity-studio, freecad, ableton, davinci-resolve, backblaze-b2.
- `generate-opencode-agents.sh:221` enables `macos-automator_*` for `mac`/`automate` agents, but neither exists as a `Task` subagent type available to Build+, and `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` has no `mac` agent entry.
- Build+ frontmatter lists `context7`, `sentry`, `socket`, `shadcn` as subagents, yet they are not invokable through Task and their MCPs cannot be connected.

After the user named the tool, the test succeeded by running AppleScript directly through `osascript`. It set `AXManualAccessibility` on the Electron process, clicked "Add project", drove NSOpenPanel through Cmd+Shift+G, and captured the window with `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` + `screencapture -l`. Workable, but it was only discovered because the user prompted for it.

Unreachable (no activation path): context7 (#32499), outscraper, dataforseo, shadcn, claude-code-mcp, macos-automator, ios-simulator, sentry, socket, cloudflare-api, openapi-search, chrome-devtools, gsc, google-analytics-mcp, amazon-order-history, MCP_DOCKER, shopify-dev-mcp. `localwp` appears in the user's MCP list, but no registry entry was found; its origin is unknown.

## How

1. For each unreachable registry entry, choose and implement one of the following:
   - Add `activationAgent` + `agentSource` + `activationGuidance` + `modelTier`, following `posthog` (`mcp-registry.mjs:313-328`) and the bounded activation in `mcp-activation-tool.mjs`.
   - Mark it explicitly CLI-only or retired (for example `activation: "none"`, `activationReason`), with a documented CLI fallback in its agent doc.
2. Priority: `macos-automator` (use `tools/automation/macos-automator.md`; macOS-only), `chrome-devtools`, `ios-simulator`, `sentry`, `socket`, `cloudflare-api`.
3. Routing: add a trigger in `reference/domain-index.md` / `reference/agent-routing.md` for "native macOS app UI test / automate a desktop app / computer-use-like interaction". Route it to the macOS automator agent, including the Electron `AXManualAccessibility` note in `tools/automation/macos-automator.md`.
4. Make Build+'s `subagents:` list match invokable agents, or document that entries are progressive-disclosure docs rather than Task targets.
5. Add a deterministic check (extend `plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`). Every registry entry must have either an activation agent or an explicit `activation: "none"` with a reason, so new MCPs cannot be silently unreachable.

## Acceptance

- Build+ can reach macos-automator through a scoped agent and run `list-apps` / `run-applescript` without globally enabling its tools.
- The registry test fails if an entry lacks both an activation path and an explicit opt-out.
- Asking Build+ to "test the native macOS dialog" routes to the automator path rather than reporting that no capability exists.

## Verification

- `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs` and the per-MCP registry tests
- Manual check: from Build+, connect macos-automator through its agent and run `list-apps`

title: bug(update): tracked .aidevops.json migration plans are never executed; auto-update warns forever
body:
## Problem

`aidevops update` detects registered projects that still track `.aidevops.json` in Git. For each one it writes a repair plan and prints a warning. Nothing ever consumes those plans, so the migration never happens: every update, and every auto-update, repeats the same warnings and nothing changes. On one maintainer machine this affects 25 projects. Users relying on auto-update never see the warnings at all.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
aidevops update
```

**Actual output** (repeated once per affected project; paths are local-only plan files):

```
[WARN] Tracked .aidevops.json requires a linked-worktree PR; repair plan: ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/project-config-migration-<cksum>.json
...
[INFO] Preserved 25 tracked project config(s); updated registration metadata only
```

A plan file contains only `{repo, files:[".aidevops.json",".gitignore"], worker_brief}`.

**Expected output**:

The first update that detects a tracked `.aidevops.json` converts the plan into automatic work. For maintainer-equivalent GitHub repos, that is one deduplicated, worker-ready, auto-dispatch issue per repo, or a PR opened directly from a fresh linked worktree. Later updates report that the work is queued or done instead of warning again. Repos without maintainer access, or with no GitHub remote, keep a single concise notice.

## Worker Guidance

- **Files:**
  - `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-project-config-lib.sh` (`_project_config_write_migration_plan`, lines 49-69), which writes the plan and warns.
  - The caller in the update flow: `rg -n "_project_config_write_migration_plan" .agents`.
- **Reference pattern:** the existing index-only migration `_project_config_migrate_linked_worktree` (same file, lines 71-78). Use `gh-write-helper.sh issue create` for managed repos, so origin labels and signatures are applied, with a stable body marker such as `<!-- aidevops:project-config-migration -->` for dedup. Check maintainer access through the same permission probe that `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` uses.
- **Constraints:**
  - Never delete the local `.aidevops.json`. The migration is `git rm --cached` plus a `.gitignore` entry only.
  - Never edit a canonical checkout; work only in linked worktrees.
  - Never put private repo names or local paths into public (aidevops) issues. Per-repo issues belong in the project's own repo.
  - Rate-limit the work: at most N repos per update run, and skip repos that already have an open marker issue or PR.
- **Verification:**
  - Add a fixture test with two registered repos that track `.aidevops.json`, one maintainer-accessible and one not. The first gets exactly one issue or PR across two update runs. The second gets one notice and no GitHub write.
  - `shellcheck` and the existing project-config tests must pass (`rg -l "project-config" .agents/scripts/tests`).

title: fix(worktree-cleanup): stop async cleanup being killed by pulse exit and expire idle deferred post-merge owners
body:
## Problem

The central worktree base (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR`) accumulates hundreds of linked worktrees (observed: 210 dirs, ~195 GB) even after their PRs merge and their sessions are closed.

## Evidence (local diagnosis, 2026-09-27)

1. **Async cleanup is killed mid-run on macOS.** `cleanup_worktrees.log` shows 5 consecutive `cleanup-worktrees-async` runs that start but never log `Completed`/`outcome=`, and `Reclaiming stale lock` appears 17 times. On macOS `_preflight_launch_async_cleanup` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`) uses `nohup ... &` without `setsid`, so the helper shares the pulse process group; launchd tears down the job's process group when `pulse-wrapper.sh` exits (no `AbandonProcessGroup`). Result: 73 worktrees (~56 GB) never evaluated in recent runs. Worker launch already uses `setsid nohup` for exactly this reason (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`, GH#21102).
2. **Deferred post-merge owners never expire while the interactive TUI lives.** `full-loop-helper.sh merge` records a deferred cleanup receipt plus a `post-merge-cleanup` registry claim owned by the interactive runtime PID. `_clean_deferred_parent_alive` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`) treats the worktree as busy for as long as that PID lives. Interactive TUIs live for hours or days and run many full-loops in sequence, so every merged worktree they touched stays (`parent-runtime-active` 37 dirs ~67 GB, `owned-skip` 21 dirs ~21 GB). One session was observed owning 4 merged worktrees after it had moved on to newer ones.

## Proposed fix

- Launch async cleanup helpers with `setsid nohup` when `setsid` exists (fallback unchanged) so the pulse exit cannot kill them.
- Expire a live deferred owner's lease when either (a) the receipt is older than `WORKTREE_DEFERRED_OWNER_MAX_HOURS` (default 4, matching `WORKTREE_CLEAN_GRACE_HOURS`), or (b) the same owner PID and non-generic session has since registered a newer worktree (the session moved on). On expiry, release only the exact `post-merge-cleanup` registry contract for that owner so the downstream guards (active cwd, dirty content, open PR, merge proof) still decide removal.

## Files

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh` — `_preflight_launch_async_cleanup` nohup fallback.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` — add lease-expiry predicate next to `full_loop_cleanup_owner_alive`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh` — `_clean_deferred_parent_alive` uses the predicate and releases the exact registry contract.
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md` + `.agents/scripts/commands/worktree-cleanup.md` — document the lease expiry.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cleanup-branch-merged-owned-skip.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-systemd-unit-generation.sh`
- `shellcheck` on edited scripts.
- After deploy: run `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`; confirm `outcome=` line, removed count > 0, and fewer `parent-runtime-active` skips.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- `archive-attribution-unclear` skips for older worker worktrees.
- Worktrees for repos absent from `repos.json` are never evaluated.
- `cleanup_worktrees.log` has no rotation (observed 367 MB).

title: Pulse/worker efficiency: false premature_exit loops, Maintainer Gate runner starvation, unbounded pulse-stats
body:
## What

Remove three measured sources of wasted pulse/worker/CI capacity found during a live efficiency review (2026-09-27, 14 open PRs, 0 active workers with 22 free slots).

## Why (evidence)

1. **False `premature_exit` continuation loops.** `output_has_completion_signal` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`) appends each `tool_use` `input.command` to `model_text`. Argv-style tools (`aidevops_bounded_operation`) pass `command` as a JSON array, so `"\n".join()` raised `TypeError`, the classifier exited non-zero, and completed runs that ended with an exact `POST_PR_HANDOFF` line were recorded as `premature_exit` and resumed. Evidence from `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`: #32495 ran 6 continuation retries after a 16-minute completed run; #32494 and #32467 (24 min) show the same pattern. All preserved excerpts re-classify as `completion=yes handoff=yes` with the fix.
2. **Hosted-runner starvation from Maintainer Gate issue events.** Job 3 (`retrigger-pr-checks` in `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml`) needed a runner for every `labeled`/`unlabeled`/`assigned` issue event. Pulse status/tier label churn produced 147 issue-event runs in ~2h; 86 of 168 queued Actions runs were Maintainer Gate, and PR `Code Quality Analysis` jobs waited ~17 minutes for a runner. Job 1's verdict only reads `needs-maintainer-review`, `origin:worker`, `origin:interactive`, `source:*` labels and assignees.
3. **Unbounded `pulse-stats.json`.** 10.2MB, 565,964 counter timestamps, 98.5% older than 7 days; every `pulse_stats_increment` re-parsed and rewrote the whole file under the stats lock, and 16 orphaned 10MB `.write-*` temps remained. The longest reader window is 7d.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh` — normalize list/tuple `command` to a string before appending.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh` — extend the existing exact-handoff test with an argv tool event.
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` — Job 3 `if:` runs only for assignment changes and verdict-relevant labels (fails open when the label name is absent).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh` — prune timestamps older than `PULSE_STATS_RETENTION_SECONDS` (default 8d, 0 disables) during increment; once per process sweep `.write-*`/`.repair-*` temps older than 60 minutes.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml`

title: Brief template write-surface label no longer matches the readiness validator, so template briefs stay publication:pending
body:
## Description

Briefs that follow `templates/brief-template.md` never pass schema-v2 readiness, so the issues they back stay `publication:pending` indefinitely and never receive `auto-dispatch` / `status:available`.

The template's "Complete Write Surface" section asks for `- **Existing verification/tests:**` (renamed in 8b30cd50d, GH#30444, 2026-08-19). The readiness validator still requires the pre-rename label `**Tests/fixtures:**` (`brief-readiness-helper.sh:325`, e9f593222). `_field_line` matches the label literally (`grep -iF "**${field}:**"`), so a template-conformant brief always reports `write-surface:Tests/fixtures` and `WORKER_READY=false`.

`planning-publication-reconcile.sh:138` gates the publication transition on `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness`. It prints `canonical task, ref, or brief validation failed; retaining publication:pending`, so the task is silently never dispatched after its planning PR merges.

## Expected Behavior

The template and the validator agree on one label (or the validator accepts both during a transition). A brief written from the current template passes `check-readiness` when its content is substantive, and default-branch reconciliation projects the intended dispatch labels.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (in a managed repository whose planning PR had merged; brief path redacted):

```
bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile --repo <owner>/<repo> --sha <default-branch-sha> --task <task-id>
bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness todo/tasks/<task-id>-brief.md
```

**Actual output**:

```
[WARNING] <task-id>/#<issue>: canonical task, ref, or brief validation failed; retaining publication:pending
WORKER_READY=false
SCORE=5
THRESHOLD=4
SCHEMA=v2
VALIDATION_ERRORS=write-surface:Tests/fixtures;write-surface:Schemas/config;write-surface:Generated/deployed mirrors;write-surface:Migrations/backfills;write-surface:Cleanup/rollback paths;acceptance:negative-regression;
```

The brief used the template's `- **Existing verification/tests:** ...` line with concrete backticked paths. Three sibling briefs from the same session failed the same way; all three issues remained `publication:pending` without dispatch labels after the planning PR merged.

**Expected output**: `WORKER_READY=true` for the write-surface verification line, or a validation error that names the label the template actually uses.

**Causal status**: confirmed (for the label mismatch).

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: default-branch issue sync → `planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile` → `_publication_validate_mapping` (`:132-140`).
- **Call chain**: `_publication_validate_mapping` → `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness` → `brief-readiness-helper.sh` `_validate_v2_body` (`:297-348`) → field loop at `:325` → `_write_surface_field_is_valid` → `_field_line` (`:162-169`, literal `**Tests/fixtures:**` match).
- **Integrated verification**: running `check-readiness` on a template-conformant brief reproduces the failure above. Relabelling only that line to `**Tests/fixtures:**` clears the `write-surface:Tests/fixtures` error.

**Causal code**:

```bash
git blame -L 325,325 origin/main -- .agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh   # e9f593222 (2026-07-12) requires "Tests/fixtures"
git blame -L 309,309 origin/main -- .agents/templates/brief-template.md        # 8b30cd50d (2026-08-19) renamed it to "Existing verification/tests"
```

**Call-site sweep** (`rg` over `.agents`, excluding tests): only these two lines use either label. Test fixtures in `scripts/tests/test-brief-readiness.sh`, `test-verify-brief.sh` and `test-brief-inline-classifier.sh` still use `Tests/fixtures`, so the suite stays green while real template-derived briefs fail.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Write a schema-v2 brief from `templates/brief-template.md`, filling every write-surface line with concrete paths.
2. Run `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness <brief>`.
3. Observe `write-surface:Tests/fixtures` although the section contains a substantive verification/tests line.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually relabelling each brief's line to `**Tests/fixtures:**` through a follow-up planning PR, then re-running `planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile` from an exact default-branch checkout.
- Rewording evidence-backed N/A lines to include one of the validator's keywords (`because`, `no existing`, and similar). The template says "evidence-backed N/A", but the validator accepts only specific keywords, so `N/A — no schema change` fails. Consider stating the accepted forms in the template comment.

## Suggested fix

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh:325`: accept `Existing verification/tests` (the template label), keeping `Tests/fixtures` as a backward-compatible alias so existing briefs still pass.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-readiness.sh`: add a fixture that uses the template's exact label, so template/validator drift fails the suite.
- Optional: the brief pre-flight that composes and files a brief should run `check-readiness` and report failures at creation time, rather than surfacing them only as a silent `publication:pending` hold after merge.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.37.4 (latest 3.37.4)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: macOS 26.6.2
- **Shell**: bash 5.3.20(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.101.0

## Additional Context

The failure is silent from the creator's side: the issue shows `publication:pending`, and nothing in the planning PR or the issue explains that readiness failed. I found the cause only by running the reconciler by hand.

title: fix(release): reap leaked aidevops-release-control worktrees from killed release helper runs
body:
## Problem

Follow-up from GH#32528. `full-loop-release-helper.sh` creates a detached control worktree `aidevops-release-control-<pid>` in the central worktree base on every invocation (`release status`, `reconcile`, `patch`...) and removes it only from its EXIT trap. Invocations killed with SIGKILL (tool timeouts, bounded-operation cancellation, process-group teardown) never run the trap, so the full checkout leaks.

Observed on one host: 54 leaked control worktrees (~150 MB each, ~8 GB) created within ~90 minutes, all registered in `git worktree list`, all with dead creating PIDs, all clean. The generic cleanup never evaluates them (detached HEAD, no branch/PR attribution).

## Fix

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` — before adding a new control worktree, reap existing `aidevops-release-control-<pid>` worktrees whose PID is dead and that have been idle 30+ minutes, via `git worktree remove --force` on the canonical repo (control worktrees are disposable snapshots; failures never block the release).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`
- Live: run `aidevops release status <pr>` once; leaked control worktrees older than 30 minutes disappear and `git worktree list` no longer lists them.

title: t18485: docs: record Stagehand v4 deterministic like-for-like benchmark
body:
## What

Record the first like-for-like Stagehand v4.1.0 against Playwright measurement in `.agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md`. It is a deterministic multi-page extraction with no AI calls. Also correct the outdated "no comparable benchmark" statement in `.agents/tools/browser/stagehand.md`.

## Why

`browser-benchmark.md:49` said a like-for-like v4 benchmark "is not yet implemented", and `stagehand.md:95` said no comparable v4/Playwright benchmark exists. A downstream award-enrichment project has since measured both engines on five public pages over three alternating rounds, collecting an identical payload. Both returned identical content. Stagehand was about 4% slower (summed medians 10.35 s against 9.95 s), with about 620 ms extra launch and attach time. Without this result, agents keep re-evaluating Stagehand for deterministic extraction.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md`: a new dated section alongside the existing v4 probes, following their pattern (method, table, limits, recommendation), and a corrected Tool Coverage row.
- `.agents/tools/browser/stagehand.md:95`: the benchmark-availability sentence.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The new section states the method, the medians table, content parity, per-page variance and scope limits, and keeps Playwright as the default.
- [ ] Regression guard: the section must not claim a full-matrix, AI-path or Playwriter comparison, and must not be compared with the v3 table.
- [ ] `linters-local.sh --changed` passes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed

```

## Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md`
- `.agents/tools/browser/stagehand.md`

<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>
